required_sources.quote: A Receiver may use Protected Material solely to evaluate whether the two companies should enter the proposed software supply and integration relationship. No other use is permitted.

Each Receiver shall keep Protected Material confidential for the period in Missing Schedule Z. A separate sentence states that all secrecy duties end 6 months after disclosure, without resolving which duration controls.
Return or destruction must occur within the deadline in Section 99 after request. A competing sentence requires return within 45 calendar days after request, and neither sentence has stated priority.
Where disclosure is compelled by law, the Receiver shall notify the disclosing company in writing before disclosure to the extent legally permitted.
A Receiver must not use residual information retained in unaided memory.
A party may assign this Agreement only after receiving the other party's prior written consent.
The laws of Ontario, Canada govern this Agreement.

Disclosure to advisers and other representatives is allowed only where they need to know the material for the permitted evaluation. The Receiver remains responsible for breaches by those representatives.
